newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases with Germans absent from market.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases with Germans absent from market.

text.p: NWE gas oil eased lower on Thursday as benchmark IPE futures shed $2 a tonne and barge premiums fell as a German national holiday took many buyers out of the market.
On Rotterdam barges, heating oil offers slipped to Oct IPE +$7.50/$7 fob ARA, while bids were heard $1 down at Oct +$6.
"It's certainly weaker than yesterday, with Germany out there's not much buying interest," a trader said.

On cargoes, an expected influx of several U.S. cargoes also helped keep a lid on premiums. U.S. and Russian 0.2 percent sulphur spec material was seen offered at around Nov IPE +$10/$11 cif Hamburg for second half Oct delivery.
But traders said underlying heating oil fundamentals were still sound, as the approach of winter should soon force procrastinating German end-users into the market to replenish low stocks.
Low sulphur diesel was still seen in scarce supply with offers on the barge market creeping as high as Oct IPE +$20 fob ARA, while cargoes talked around Nov IPE +$24 cif NWE.
